scope: Re-examination of the v2.0 G4 PASS. No historical record was modified; no threshold changed.

summary.why: device_capability() treated cuda_available=false as proof of CPU-only hardware. On this host cuda_available=false only because the binary was built without CUDA; the machine physically has an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050. CUDA build/runtime availability is not physical GPU absence.

method_1_os_device_inventory.conclusion: A discrete NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 (~4.0 GiB) is physically present, in addition to integrated Intel UHD graphics.

method_2_production_profiler.provenance: source: EnumDisplayDevices display-adapter enumeration | adapters: Intel(R) UHD Graphics | Intel(R) UHD Graphics | Intel(R) UHD Graphics | Intel(R) UHD Graphics | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050
method_2_production_profiler.conclusion: The production profiler independently reports physical GPU presence, matching the OS device inventory. The two sources agree.

physical_hardware_evidence.spec_confirmation: design/V009_phase1_M0_specification.md names the target hardware as 'HP Victus: i5-12450H, RTX 2050 4 GB VRAM, 24 GB RAM'. The recovered records' CPU (i5-12450H) matches this target.

how_the_fields_are_populated_today.collectGpu(): When compiled without CUDA (STARK_P1_CUDA_COMPILED undefined): cuda_available=false; provenance['cuda_available']='unavailable: binary built without CUDA (STARK_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF / no toolkit)'; gpu_model='unavailable: binary built without CUDA'; cuda_version likewise. vram_total_bytes is left unset.
how_the_fields_are_populated_today.meaning: These are BUILD facts, not hardware facts. They cannot distinguish 'no GPU' from 'no CUDA in this build'.

the_defect.old_logic: if cuda_available is a bool: return true? GPU : CPU  -- i.e. cuda_available=false => CPU-only
the_defect.consequence: A CUDA-disabled build on a GPU host was classified CPU-only, which let the recovered records bypass the measured-VRAM requirement and produced the v2.0 G4 PASS.

frozen_spec_context.G4_definition: Every baseline record's peak RAM/VRAM comes from process/device queries (B8), with measured: true; any estimated field is flagged and gate G4 fails if a peak memory field is estimated.
frozen_spec_context.G3_definition: If CUDA exists: GPU baselines produce complete records; if no CUDA: records exist with status: skipped + reason. Either branch passes.
frozen_spec_context.note: G3 keys on CUDA availability (a build fact) and legitimately permits skip records. G4 keys on measured peak RAM/VRAM. The physical-capability question is separate from both.

files.change: Added std::optional<bool> gpu_present to StaticHardwareProfile (tri-state physical presence: true / false / nullopt=unknown), documented as independent of cuda_available.

Added collectPhysicalGpuPresence(): on Windows, EnumDisplayDevices enumeration of display adapters (real vs basic/remote); sets gpu_present and provenance. Serialize/parse gpu_present (bare bool when known, {value:null,reason} when unknown). Non-Windows => nullopt + reason.

Rewrote device_capability(): GPU if gpu_present==true / cuda_available==true / authoritative GPU field; CPU ONLY if gpu_present==false; else Unknown. cuda_available==false is no longer CPU-only evidence. Updated the fail-closed detail string.
E2/B4/B5 SKIPPED reason made build-scoped and precise: states CUDA is unavailable in THIS build without asserting the machine lacks a GPU, and points to hardware.gpu_present.
mk() helper now declares confirmed CPU-only via gpu_present=false; added 6 v2.1 capability regression blocks (12 new checks). 328 -> 340 assertions.
Controlled CPU-workload fixtures now set hardware.gpu_present=false explicitly (no longer relying on a CUDA-less build flag).
New generator for the three v2.1 capability fixtures.

source_change.no_threshold_or_schema_break: No frozen threshold, grouping key, or historical record changed. The added hardware field is additive.

nine_recovered_records.reason: records carry cuda_available=false and no gpu_present evidence; physical capability is Unknown -> fail closed ('refusing to classify as CPU-only')

v2_1_candidate_evidence.input: archive_recovery/v21_evidence/ (9 recovered + genuine PROFILE/TELEMETRY + genuine E2/B4/B5 skip = 14 records)
v2_1_candidate_evidence.reason: E5 (and E1) still lack gpu_present evidence -> Unknown -> fail closed. Even had they carried gpu_present=true, the CUDA-less build cannot measure VRAM, so the measured-VRAM requirement would still fail.

corrected_result.verdict: G4 is FAIL. The v2.0 G4 PASS is withdrawn.

regression_tests_added: Physical GPU present, CUDA build disabled (gpu_present=true, cuda_available=false), VRAM unavailable -> G4 FAIL
Physical GPU present, CUDA enabled (gpu_present=true, cuda_available=true, gpu_model), VRAM measured -> G4 PASS
Confirmed CPU-only (gpu_present=false, cuda_available=false), documented VRAM unavailability -> G4 PASS (CPU workload, frozen rule)
Unknown capability: cuda_available=false alone (no gpu_present) -> G4 FAIL (must not be read as CPU-only)
Unknown capability: gpu_present present but malformed/null-valued -> G4 FAIL
GPU workload requiring VRAM: gpu_present=true, vram_measured=true but VRAM value unavailable -> G4 FAIL

backward_compatibility.existing_records: Preserved unchanged. Records predating the gpu_present field have no physical-capability evidence; they are now classified Unknown and fail G4 closed.
backward_compatibility.migration_limitation: There is no way to retroactively derive physical GPU presence for a historical record that did not capture it. Such records cannot regain a CPU-only classification and cannot satisfy the measured-VRAM requirement either; they remain G4-FAIL by construction. This is intentional (fail closed) and is the honest handling of the frozen rule.
backward_compatibility.schema: Additive only. Older readers ignore gpu_present; older records parse with gpu_present absent (Unknown).
